title: Installing jQuery Using npm
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of installing jquery using npm in a jQuery application.
Apply introduction to npm packages in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify installing the jquery package with an explicit test or browser observation.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through installing jquery using npm with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns introduction to npm packages into a repeatable implementation choice. A page must load one compatible jQuery build before dependent application code runs. Keep the chosen version explicit and verify the loaded file in the browser Network and Console panels.

task_acceptance_criteria: The implementation demonstrates installing jquery using npm using a current, documented approach.
The learner records the expected and actual behavior and checks at least one edge case.
The example preserves semantic HTML and does not render untrusted data as HTML.
The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.
hints: First identify which DOM nodes and runtime state are involved in installing jquery using npm.
Make one small change, inspect the resulting element or request, and compare it with the expected result.
If the result differs, check the selector, script order, browser console, event target, and relevant API documentation before adding more code.
content.expected_output: The install command adds jQuery 4.0.0 to the project; the version check should print 4.0.0 in a compatible Node package context.
common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
